newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia at odds with oil JVs on export levels.
newsitem.headline: Russia at odds with oil JVs on export levels.

text.p: Russia is at odds with some prominent Western joint ventures over how much crude oil they export, with state customs officials calling on Friday for fines on outfits they say are exporting beyond their limits.

Vladimir Chuvayev, head of energy tariffs at the State Customs Committee, told Reuters that four big joint ventures -- White Nights, KomiArcticOil, Mekamineft and Tatex -- could be hit with a total of $20 million in fines.
"The companies have already protested against this and now it is up to the committee to decide," Chuvayev said.
But a KomiArcticOil official said the fines were unjustified.
"We are keeping cool and hope the customs committee will rule that we are the right party in the dispute," Kirill Skidan, KomiArcticOil's marketing director, said.
"We have been exporting oil for five years without any claims from customs and the issue was probably raised to justify the existence of the energy tariffs section and show that it really works."
KomiArcticOil groups British Gas Plc, the Komineft oil firm and Ukhtaneftegazgeologiya, a geological outfit.
Officials at White Nights, a 50-50 joint venture between Phibro Energy Production Inc and SIDANKO unit Varyoganneftegaz, were not available for comment.
Tatex includes U.S. Texneft Inc, while Mekamineft involves Germany's Katoil GmbH.
Chuvayev said the fines were in order because the four were exporting more than allowed under a 1994 government decree.

Russia's oil joint ventures have said they must retain the right to export most if not all their output in order to survive the numerous and ever-changing taxes Russia imposes on them. They also say they must retain priority access to Russia's crowded oil pipeline system.
Chuvayev said a Fuel and Energy Ministry order in March allowed all joint ventures to freely export their oil if their oilwells were part of their fixed capital and not rented.

KomiArcticOil and White nights own their oilwells, but Chuvayev said they and the other two outfits must pay fines on 1995 exports which exceeded what he termed their "basic" output, which he said should be partly sold to the state at lower prices.
Chuvayev said KomiArcticOil exceeded its duty-free export limits last year by 270,000 tonnes, White Nights by 214,000 tonnes, Mekamineft by 310,000 tonnes and Tatex by 36,000 tonnes.
The four joint ventures are a handful of the nearly 50 ventures with foreign capital that are producing and exporting oil from Russia.
